questions.question: How do partials and layouts work in Rails views?
questions.title: Partials and Layouts
questions.direct_answer: Partials are reusable view snippets: a file named with a leading underscore (_form.html.erb) rendered with render 'form' (Rails drops the underscore and extension). They DRY up repeated view code — the same form for new and edit. Layouts are the page shell that wraps an action's view: app/views/layouts/application.html.erb has the <head>, nav, and <%= yield %> where the action's content goes. Every action renders inside the layout by default. You can pick a layout (layout 'admin') or render a partial from anywhere (render 'shared/nav'). Partials + layouts let you compose pages from shared pieces without repeating HTML.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know partials are _name files rendered with render 'name' (DRY repeated views) and layouts wrap the action with yield.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Naming a partial without the leading underscore (render looks for _form.html.erb), or forgetting yield in the layout (no action content shows).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Partials are _name.html.erb files, rendered with render 'name' (DRY repeated views). Layouts wrap the action with <%= yield %>. Compose pages from shared pieces.
